summary: Phase 149O.20L.1B -- HMRC-001 v1.1 HMIC Contract-Identity Alignment Independent Verification (149O.20L.1B). Independently re-derived the whole 149O.20L.1A repair chain from fixed git history and current primary source, trusting neither 149O.20L.1A's report, its own tests, its Outcome-B classification, its claim that derive_contract_versions was never stale, its claim that HMIC-REQ-067/069 were already correct, its same-version repair rationale, nor its historical-test attribution. Confirmed the real end-to-end validator -- not a bare Python dict comparison -- fails closed to CertificationStatus.CONTRACT_MISMATCH on contract-version drift, via direct inspection of the real validator's Step 10 source and the pre-existing (149O.19.5D-era, unmodified by either 149O.20L.1A or this phase) TestContractMismatch::test_contract_version_drift_rejected suite, which exercises the full validator against a record with a drifted HMRC-001 entry. Reconstructed 149O.20L.1A's exact repair diff (90e14496..7eb9afb4) via git diff: exactly two files changed (the HMIC-001 contract file and 149O.20L.1A's own new test module); within the contract file, only the header block (Status/Repaired-by/Depends-on lines) and a new, purely descriptive Section 54 were added; zero HMIC-REQ-### line was removed or renumbered; HMRC-001 remained byte-identical across the repair commit. Concluded independently: Outcome B confirmed -- the normative HMIC-REQ-067/069 mechanism and production's derive_contract_versions were never stale; the sole defect was HMIC-001's own descriptive Depends-on header line. Independently adjudicated the same-version repair valid: the 149O.20D.1 precedent this repair mirrors was itself a same-version repair (HMIC-001 stayed v1.2) despite widening a normative requirement's file count from 24 to 25 -- a strictly larger semantic change than 149O.20L.1A's pure header-and-descriptive-history edit, which changed zero HMIC-REQ-### semantics; a repair that changes no requirement meaning at all is a fortiori valid staying same-version. Both new failures were individually re-run in isolation with full tracebacks captured and independently classified as self-inflicted test fragility, not a mechanism regression: test_phase_149o_20d_hmic_v1_2_hbdc_bound_contract_identity_evolution.py::test_depends_on_line_lists_hbdc fails with ValueError: substring not found, a 149O.20D-era test hardcoding the exact old Depends-on label text ('unamended, byte-unchanged'), which 149O.20L.1A's repair legitimately reworded to '(current, HMIC-unamended)'; test_phase_149o_20k_3_hmic_class_b_verifier_production_source_set_alignment_independent_verification.py::TestByteIdentitySinceK2Entry::test_hmic_contract_byte_unchanged_since_k2_entry fails with an AssertionError on a fixed-commit byte-identity comparison against the 149O.20K.2 entry commit -- structurally guaranteed to fail after any future HMIC-001 edit, independent of this specific repair's content.
